Thirty-first daf of the Rashi content-quality reconstruction campaign (26 raw lines, 16 legal ids). Continuing the freshly-confirmed queue after 67a (69a, 69b, 70b, 71a all confirmed zero-link rashi-reconstruction targets; 67b needs no work).

Built a definitive line-by-line skeleton for all 26 vilna lines before writing any English, re-extracting the raw Hebrew fresh from the packet. Content covers: why the Mishnah's second clause about placing tefillin under the head was needed and Rav Pappa's/Rav Mesharshiya's refinement to 'alongside the head' (l01, l02, vilna 1-4); the resolution of the shatnez concern for the High Priest's linen belt via the view that it is the same belt worn by the ordinary priest year-round (l11, vilna 5-10); Rav Ashi's alternative resolution that the priestly garments are too stiff to constitute shatnez, illustrated by Rav Huna's felt-mat ruling (l22, vilna 11-15); the beraita distinguishing wearing priestly garments in the Temple (permitted) from the provinces (forbidden, since worn in a mundane manner there) (l25, vilna 16-17); Mount Gerizim as the Samaritans' dwelling place (l27, vilna 17-18); the 'time to act for the Lord' principle permitting Torah suspension (l41, vilna 18-20); and Abaye's ruling that the synagogue attendant taking the Torah scroll in the deputy's/head's presence, even though ordinarily a student may not act in a master's presence, is entirely for the sake of the High Priest's honor, not a genuine exception to the honor-of-the-master rule (l42, vilna 20-25).

Seven of the sixteen local segment ids (l07, l15, l19, l28, l32, l35, l38) receive no Rashi comment on this daf at all: l07 (the Gemara's own shatnez objection, self-explanatory), l15 (the spreading-versus-wearing distinction, self-explanatory), l19 (the ten-mattresses proof, self-explanatory), and the entire l28/l32/l35/l38 block, which is the extended Aggadic narrative of Shimon HaTzaddik meeting Alexander the Great and the Samaritans' plot against the Temple - a vivid but linguistically straightforward narrative passage that draws no separate gloss anywhere in the raw Hebrew. Confirmed by scanning all 26 raw lines for any of that narrative's distinctive vocabulary (Alexander, Shimon HaTzaddik, the prostration episode, the impaling and plowing of Mount Gerizim) and finding none, consistent with the established pattern of narrative Gemara sections sometimes receiving zero Rashi commentary.

Four raw lines are genuine dibbur-boundary straddles where Rashi's own comment closes one lemma and opens the next within the same print line: line 16 (l22/l25), line 17 (l25/l27), line 18 (l27/l41), and line 20 (l41/l42). Audit_rashi_association.py's multi_link count (4) was checked against this prediction before proceeding; declared_associations=30=22*1+4*2, matching exactly.

The daf's final raw line (26, the single word 'ein,' 'indeed') is a genuine deferred dibbur hamatchil, most plausibly opening Rashi's comment on the Mishnah's 'and the High Priest stands' (l44, the last id in this packet), which implies he ordinarily sits; boundary policy assigns it there, and the notes flag it as continuing on 69b's own Rashi rather than asserting a specific completion (69b's own reconstruction, not yet done, was not used to verify this, unlike the 66b-to-67a and 67a-to-67b deferrals earlier in the campaign which had an already-built neighbor to check against).

Unlike every other daf reconstructed so far this campaign, 69a's raw Rashi contains ZERO citation anchors of any kind (0 found, 0 missing, both before and after this edit): no tractate name, daf/amud number, chapter, or verse reference appears anywhere in the 26 lines. Classification is INSUFFICIENT-ANCHORS and cannot become ALIGNED. Confirmed via the drift-profile scanner and an independent full manual reread of all 26 lines; the zeroAnchorAttestation block above confirms no citation was invented, moved, or duplicated and no semantic uncertainty remains.
